previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: An elderly woman with chronic diastolic heart failure, recurrent venous thromboembolism on warfarin, chronic abdominal pain, and anemia was admitted for lower abdominal pain and dark stools. She had not had a bowel movement in five days, and imaging showed diverticulosis without acute diverticulitis. Her hemoglobin was 6.5 g/dL, and she received two units of packed red blood cells for acute on chronic anemia. She was found to have hyponatremia and hypokalemia. A urine culture grew enterococcus, and she was discharged on a five-day course of amoxicillin. Pulmonary edema was treated with diuresis, and repeat imaging showed improvement, though she required home oxygen due to persistent desaturations with activity. Warfarin was held during admission due to melena and not restarted at discharge. She was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up planned for anemia, anticoagulation, and infection resolution.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic heart failure
Urinary tract infection, site not specified
Diverticulosis of colon (without mention of hemorrhage)
Personal history of venous thrombosis and embolism

Brief Hospital Course:
Ms ___ presents with malaise and was found to have low HCT 
(13.6) with no obvious bleeding sources.   
.
# Anemia:
EGD and colonoscopy previously revealed gastritis / diverticula, 
but had no bleeding on prior evaluation from these sites.   
Guiaic negative in ED this admission.   It's possible that her 
HCT, in the setting of leukopenia, represents a 
hypoproliferative bone marrow, with slow drift down in HCT over 
the last several months, when she last presented and was 
transfused. CTA abdomen shows no active extravasation.    She 
had missed three outpatient hematology appointments, so she was 
evaluated by the inpatient hematology service.  They advised B12 
supplementation (although MMA returned as normal on day of 
discharge).  It is possible that she has MDS, but she is not a 
candidate for tx.  She will followup with hematology as an 
outpatient.  She received three units of PRBC and her hematocrit 
increased appropriately and she had significant improvement in 
energy level.

# Abdominal pain -  Chronic.  Per last hospitalization, appears 
to be partially functional pain (distractable).  Negative UA, CT 
abd negative
.

improved with IV lasix in house.  Patient without dyspnea at 
rest; does have very poor functional status and does have DOE, 
but unclear if this is from CHF vs reconditioning.  She appears 
to be at her functional baseline per family.
.
# Recurrent DVT:  Resumed coumadin as she does not have an iron 
deficiency anemia and there was no evidence of GI bleeding.  Per 
family, she is not bridged when INR is sub therapeutic.

FINDINGS: 

VASCULAR:

There is no abdominal aortic aneurysm. There is moderate calcium burden in the
abdominal aorta and great abdominal arteries.  The there is a replaced right
hepatic artery arising off the aorta adjacent the celiac axis.  The celiac
axis and SMA are widely patent, as is the ___.

LOWER CHEST: The imaged lung bases demonstrate chronic interstitial
abnormalities in association with ground glass opacities bilaterally, and
trace pleural fluid on the left.  There is no focal consolidation suggest
pneumonia.  Heart size is enlarged and there is no pericardial effusion.

ABDOMEN:
The liver is homogeneous in attenuation aside from a focal area of hypodensity
adjacent to the falciform ligament, a classic location for focal fatty
infiltration.  There is no intrahepatic biliary dilation and the portal and
hepatic veins are patent.  The gallbladder is normal with no stones.  The
pancreas is normal in attenuation with no duct dilation or surrounding
stranding.  The spleen is normal in size and attenuation.  The adrenal glands
are morphologically normal bilaterally.  The kidneys enhance symmetrically
with no hydronephrosis or perinephric abnormality.  Hypodensity at the upper
pole of the right kidney corresponds to a simple cyst.

The distal esophagus, stomach, and small bowel are normal in caliber.  There
is no focus of extravasation which in the large bowel, however there are
several diverticula throughout the colon.  No evidence of diverticulitis.  The
appendix is not visualized but there are no secondary signs appendicitis.  No
mesenteric or retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy.  No intra-abdominal free air or
free fluid.

PELVIS: The urinary bladder is normal.  The uterus and adnexae are
unremarkable.  No pelvic lymphadenopathy or free fluid.

BONES: There is a left total hip arthroplasty with no evidence of
periprosthetic fracture.  Osseous structures are demineralized.  Multilevel
degenerative changes throughout the lumbar spine are unchanged from ___. 
There is mild levoconvex scoliosis of the thoracolumbar spine.  No concerning
osseous lesion.

1. Several colonic diverticula, the most numerous in the sigmoid colon,
however no evidence of active extravasation in the small or large bowel.
2. Chronic interstitial abnormality at the lung bases bilaterally, not
significantly changed from the prior exam in ___. Moderate cardiomegaly and moderate atherosclerotic calcification of the
abdominal aorta.
